patterns.usage_note: The formal written counterpart of で for the place, time, or domain in which something takes place (国際[こくさい]会議[かいぎ]において, 教育[きょういく]の分野[ぶんや]において). It does not take over で's other jobs: tool, material, and cause stay with で (はさみで切[き]る, 風邪[かぜ]で休[やす]む). Used of everyday activities it sounds stilted, so keep it for documents, announcements, and academic prose. における／においての is the shape used before a noun.

examples.ruby: 開会式[かいかいしき]は市民[しみん]ホールにおいて行[おこな]われる。
examples.english: The opening ceremony will be held at the civic hall.

examples.ruby: 医療[いりょう]の分野[ぶんや]において、人工知能[じんこうちのう]の活用[かつよう]が進[すす]む。
examples.english: In the medical field, the use of artificial intelligence is advancing.

examples.ruby: 当社[とうしゃ]は品質[ひんしつ]において他社[たしゃ]に劣[おと]らない。
examples.english: In terms of quality, our company yields to no competitor.

patterns.usage_note: A literary 〜で inherited from classical Japanese and now alive mainly in set expressions: 一夜[いちや]にして and 一瞬[いっしゅん]にして for a change that lands all at once, 今[いま]にして思[おも]えば for a realization that arrives only in hindsight, and an age or an ordinal for a point reached strikingly early or late (四十[しじゅう]にして, 三度目[さんどめ]にして). A note of surprise or admiration comes with it, so a plain "in／at" is better carried by において or で. Nouns only, and rare outside writing and these fixed turns.

examples.ruby: その街[まち]は一夜[いちや]にして灰[はい]と化[か]した。
examples.english: That town was reduced to ashes overnight.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]にして思[おも]えば、あれは別[わか]れの言葉[ことば]だった。
examples.english: Looking back on it now, those were words of farewell.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]は四十[しじゅう]にして初[はじ]めて筆[ふで]を執[と]った。
examples.english: It was at forty that he first took up the pen.

patterns.usage_note: The everyday particle for the setting an action takes place in, and the default wherever において, にあって, or にして would sound ceremonial. The same で also marks means, material, cause, and scope (バスで行[い]く, 木[き]で作[つく]る, 病気[びょうき]で休[やす]む), duties its stiffer relatives in this family do not take on. With verbs of existence (いる／ある) and with location of residence, the place takes に (家[いえ]にいる), not で. で is neutral for means; によって is chosen when the means is a deliberate method or procedure, and is obligatory for the agent of a passive.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]で友[とも]だちと待[ま]ち合[あ]わせた。
examples.english: I met up with my friend in front of the station.

examples.ruby: 昨日[きのう]はカフェで三時間[さんじかん]も勉強[べんきょう]した。
examples.english: Yesterday I studied at a cafe for a good three hours.

examples.ruby: 母[はは]は台所[だいどころ]で味噌汁[みそしる]を作[つく]っている。
examples.english: My mother is making miso soup in the kitchen.
